_doc: THE GRAVITY PROTOTYPE (SW-83, his third word; RUNNING_LOG §273): ONE gravity moment in ONE hand, with a few lead-in and lead-out notes of the same hand, nothing of the other hand. The workshop's page 'prototype' is drawn from this file. page = the IR the notes are read from · hand L|R · window = what the page shows · arc: t0 = the first note of the cluster, bounce = the impact, t1 = the last note · in / out = which notes stand on which side of the impact (the AI's first reading — HIS TO DECIDE; 'could be all on one side') · the arc's shape is the lineage's GC (notation/lib/gc.js: fall 1 - u^p, rebound to `damping` %) with the registry's preset, the fall lasting t0 -> bounce and the rebound bounce -> t1. — §297 (his word, SW-92): THE THREE-PART PROTOTYPE on this one page: (1) this gesture, its span UNCHANGED, the ribbon now across the grand staff and drawn by the designed profile of §296; (2) the repeated notes between, not yet drawn; (3) the scattered strike's curtain over the burst's notes (`also`), with its pebbles.

flow._note: §282: the inner movement ON the arc. style ribbon = the arc a ribbon, its width the busyness (from the GC line's own width up to ribbonMaxPx at the busiest); style strobe = a tick across the arc per played event, tickPx long (the page "prototype: strobe"); style strip = §279's filled curve under the staff, set aside. The busyness: each played note a bell sigmaS seconds wide and as tall as its loudness, summed, stretched between its low and high over the arc, raised to `power`.

profile._note: §296 — HIS DESIGN for this gesture (the playing only suggests): the fall a hair while the arc is almost level, growing with the drop all the way down to the greatest width; the rebound begins at that width ("a lot of activity"), goes to none, and ends at a medium width. in "depth" = the width follows how far the arc has dropped (to the power inPower); out = [how far up the rebound 0 … 1, width 0 … 1], eased between.

shapeRule._note: §276 · §279 (the AI's rule, his to move): shape 1 = the pitches up to AND WITH the impact; shape 2 = the pitches after it, drawn only when the two sets differ by changeMin pitches or more (added + dropped), its box BEGINNING afterImpact of the way up the rising arc — never at the impact (his word)
shapeRule._clusterNote: §277 (his word: clusters as a bar with noteheads on top and bottom, the actual top and bottom note, with accidentals): a shape of clusterMinNotes or more pitches with no gap over clusterMaxGap semitones is a CLUSTER BAR — its lowest and highest note and a bar between their centers, clusterBarW of a head wide (piece 2's cluster bar, NOTATION_SYSTEM_PLAN §17e.1, was one head wide and had no heads; the narrower width is the AI's, his to move)

also._note: §291: the burst that follows the flow, both hands — plain heads at their played times on their own staves (the same spans as bank/burst_proto.json). The picture shows both staves for it (band); the arc keeps its own lane on the lower staff (arcBand).

curtain._note: §296 · §298 · §299 — THE SCATTERED STRIKE: a transparent block over the stretch where the strike's notes fall (padSs each side, at least minSs wide; the grand staff and overSs beyond each staff), and a HANDFUL OF PEBBLES thrown in it. The pebbles: species and sizePx (synthesi-alpha's substrates, tools/substrate.js), density = how many. THE THROW is ballistic: each pebble a parabola lasting about flightS seconds (flightSpread = how much the pebbles' flight times differ, as a share), landing about the IMPACT — the moment the cursor reaches the curtain's middle — scattered across the floor by landSpread (a share of the curtain's width); one bounce keeping `bounce` of the speed, then still.
